activities.summary: UAE DIFC sourcing pass: good fit but disqualified as a near-term opportunity by a recent (May 2024) Broadridge IMS go-live with no dissatisfaction signal found. Recorded as nurture rather than pursued now, per the ICP's 'mid-implementation of a competitor' disqualify guidance. Revisit in 12-18 months or if a complaint/departure signal surfaces.

contacts.title: Founding Partner, Senior Executive Officer & Director

description: Independent, investment-team-owned MENA asset manager established 2014 (with roots in Amwal AlKhaleej), DIFC-regulated by the DFSA and, via a Riyadh subsidiary (Amwal Capital Almaliyah, set up 2023), CMA-regulated in Saudi Arabia. Manages capital for global sovereign wealth funds, funds of funds, multi-family offices, pensions, endowments, insurers and foundations, with a long-biased MENA public-equities strategy plus alternative-investment lines. In May 2024 the firm went live on Broadridge's investment management platform (portfolio, order and risk management, analytics and performance attribution) — a recently deployed incumbent system.

fit.reasoning: Fit 60/60: priority asset-manager segment (20) + UAE (15) + MENA public equities plus alternatives, reasonably multi-asset (10) + manages third-party institutional/SWF/MFO money (10) + DFSA-regulated (5). Trigger 0/25: no positive trigger — the one dated event found (May 2024) is a competitor implementation: Amwal went live on Broadridge's portfolio/order/risk-management platform, which is a negative signal for near-term displacement, not a buying trigger. Per the ICP's disqualify guidance ('already mid-implementation of a competitor, with no dissatisfaction signal'), this is not a live opportunity today. Access 8/15: named Founding Partner/COO (Samer Sarraf) quoted directly in the Broadridge release. Total 68 (Strong fit) but nurture — watch for any sign of dissatisfaction with the Broadridge deployment 18-24 months on, or for the separate Riyadh entity's own technology decisions.
